title: Protobuf request parsing: a body that spells one field both snake_case and camelCase is rejected with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE before any handler or validator acts
answers: Why does the server return 400 'Request specifies both secret_id and secretId' when I send a gateway secret update?
Where is the check that stops a JSON body with both proto-name and JSON-name keys from being parsed?
Does the duplicate-key guard also apply to workspace create and update requests?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_request_message, the single protobuf parse point for proto-backed REST endpoints (tracking, gateway secrets, model definitions, endpoints, scorers, and so on), and mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_workspace_request_message for workspace create/update bodies.
Rule: Both parsers call mlflow/server/handlers.py:_reject_conflicting_field_aliases on the raw JSON before parse_dict. It rejects any object that contains a field's proto name and its JSON name (for example secret_id and secretId, default_artifact_root and defaultArtifactRoot), in either key order, and recurses into nested message lists such as model_configs. Map fields and google.protobuf well-known types are skipped because their keys are caller-chosen.
Symptom: A body that supplied both spellings was authorized by a raw-key validator against one gateway secret while the handler, parsing the same body through the proto, acted on the other, so a user with READ only on a secret could update it.
Constraints: ParseDict silently lets the later key win, so any new protobuf parser added to handlers.py must go through the same guard or the split returns. A body with only one spelling of each field is unaffected; the guard does not change which spelling is accepted.
applies: Basic-auth and non-auth REST request bodies that map to protobuf messages in mlflow/server/handlers.py; not for query-string parameters read by _get_request_param.
says: Updating a gateway secret fails with an error about conflicting field names.
API requests fail when sending properties in both camel case and underscore notation.
Workspace creation request is rejected because the payload contains duplicate attribute aliases.
Prevent read-only users from modifying credentials through conflicting request property spellings.
search: In mlflow/server/handlers.py, _get_request_message and _get_workspace_request_message call _reject_conflicting_field_aliases on raw JSON before parse_dict to reject requests providing both proto and JSON field names with INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE. The check recurses into nested message lists like model_configs but skips map fields and google.protobuf well-known types. It applies to REST request bodies mapping to protobuf messages including tracking, gateway secrets, endpoints, scorers, and workspace operations, but not query-string parameters in _get_request_param.
